reading.body:
Five of the seven AI presentation tools in this dataset are US-jurisdiction products, one is registered in Germany, and one in India, a distribution that reflects where venture-backed generative AI tooling has concentrated rather than where presentation software is consumed.

The tools share a narrow functional core: text or prompt input converted to structured slides, with automated layout and design as the default value proposition. Decktopus and Presentations.AI add notes about data exposure and content governance respectively, which are the only signals in this dataset that vendors have begun treating enterprise data handling as a differentiator. The remaining tools carry no such annotation, meaning either the issue is absent or the data simply does not record it.

What this dataset does not cover is compute footprint. Presentation generation is inference-light compared to image synthesis or large-scale language tasks, and nothing here connects these tools to power consumption, data center location, or GPU demand. Pitch AI's EU-hosted note is the single infrastructure-adjacent fact in the set, and it speaks to data residency rather than energy or capacity. Readers looking for supply-chain depth, from grid to building to chip to model, will not find it in this category.
